review_note: A coproduct of algebraic spaces is an algebraic space when an étale surjective atlas from the coproduct of individual schemes fits in the chosen big site. Independently reviewed the pinned original theorem statement embedded in Stage A against the reconstructed standalone formulation; no proofs/remarks opened. Preliminary verdict only.
statement:
An **algebraic space** $F/S$ is a sheaf of sets on the chosen big fppf site $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ whose diagonal $F\to F\times F$ is representable and which admits an étale, surjective morphism $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$; 'surjective' here refers to the representable-morphism property.

Let $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ be algebraic spaces over $S$. **Sufficient size condition:** choose surjective étale atlases $U_i\to F_i$ with $\coprod_i U_i$ isomorphic to an object in the chosen fppf site $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. Under this condition, the coproduct $\coprod_i F_i$ in fppf sheaves is an algebraic space over $S$. This does not assert an arbitrary-size coproduct is representable.
hypotheses:
Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Suppose given a set $I$ and algebraic spaces $F_i$, $i \in I$.
conclusions:
Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Suppose given a set $I$ and algebraic spaces $F_i$, $i \in I$.
Then $F = \coprod_{i \in I} F_i$ is an algebraic space
provided $I$, and the $F_i$ are not too ``large'': for example if we
can choose surjective \'etale morphisms $U_i \to F_i$ such that
$\coprod_{i \in I} U_i$ is isomorphic to an object of
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, then $F$ is an algebraic space.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces}
Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Suppose given a set $I$ and algebraic spaces $F_i$, $i \in I$.
Then $F = \coprod_{i \in I} F_i$ is an algebraic space
provided $I$, and the $F_i$ are not too ``large'': for example if we
can choose surjective \'etale morphisms $U_i \to F_i$ such that
$\coprod_{i \in I} U_i$ is isomorphic to an object of
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, then $F$ is an algebraic space.

review_note: A sheaf covered by open immersions from algebraic-space subfunctors is an algebraic space if the coproduct of those subfunctors meets the size condition. statement:
An **algebraic space** $F/S$ is a sheaf of sets on the chosen big fppf site $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ whose diagonal $F\to F\times F$ is representable and which admits an étale, surjective morphism $h_U\to F$ from a scheme $U/S$; 'surjective' here refers to the representable-morphism property.

Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is a sheaf,
\item there exists an index set $I$
and subfunctors $F_i \subset F$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item each $F_i$ is an algebraic space,
\item each $F_i \to F$ is representable,
\item each $F_i \to F$ is an open immersion (see
Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}),
\item the map $\coprod F_i \to F$ is surjective as a map of sheaves, and
\item $\coprod F_i$ is an algebraic space (set theoretic condition, see
Lemma \ref{lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.
